q: Friday 16:00, the base is in sight and the tank is at three-quarters. Where do you take the boat first?
answer: A — fill up, then berth at B and report to the base
why: Full to full: the boat comes back with full tanks; refuelling by the base is charged on top of the fuel.

q: Monday 18:00, the quay attendant waves you to the free space at A. What do you do with the briefing's note?
answer: Ask for B, or anchor at C; the ferry wash will throw you onto the quay twice a day
why: The briefing's harbour notes are the base's own experience of its boats damaged on that quay; the attendant fills spaces.

figure.note: Briefing: ferry wash on the N quay 07:00 and 19:00

q: Monday 18:00, N 3 and dying, your crew want A: it is flat calm and closest to the taverna. What do you do?
answer: Anchor at B — the briefing's gusts come after dark in exactly this wind, however calm it looks now
why: Katabatic gusts fall from the cliffs after dark in a northerly; the briefing names that bay so that you do not learn it at 02:00.

q: The base manager shows you the plan for Friday. Where and how do you bring the boat back?
answer: Stern-to at B on the lazy line, by 17:00 on Friday
why: The base takes the boat back where and how the briefing says: its own berth, the lazy line, no anchor, on time.

q: Monday, 17:00, a town quay with no lazy lines; you will go in stern-to between two boats. Where do you drop the anchor?
answer: At B: about four boat lengths out, square to the gap, then reverse in
why: Four boat lengths in 5 m gives real scope and still reaches the quay with chain to spare; too close and it never bites.

labels: town quay · gap between two boats

q: Monday, 12:30, you come into a clear-water bay for lunch. Where do you drop the anchor?
answer: B: on the pale sand, where the anchor digs in and you can see it
why: An anchor skids over thick weed and jams in rock; in clear water the pale sand is the holding ground.

q: Wednesday, 17:00, near Göcek. The bay is filling up and the boats along the shore lie on anchors with lines ashore. Where do you go?
answer: B: drop well out and back in, with a long line to the shore like the others
why: Boats on lines ashore do not swing; a free-swinging boat among them hits one at the first wind shift — do as they do.

ru.shore · boats on lines ashore: берег · яхты с концами на берег

q: Friday afternoon you are approaching the base. The briefing said return berths are assigned on arrival. What do you do?
answer: Call the base on the VHF or phone before entering and take the berth they give you
why: The return berth, the time and the mooring are the base's; 'back at the base' means alongside, before the deadline.

figure.note: Friday 16:30 · contract: alongside at the base by 18:00

ru.Friday 16:30 · contract: alongside at th: Пятница 16:30 · договор: у причала базы к 18:00

q: Friday 15:30, the fuel gauge shows half. The base has given you berth B for the night. Where do you go first?
answer: Fuel dock A: fill the tank and keep the receipt, then berth B
why: 'Returned full' is in the contract; the base's own refuelling adds a service charge, and the receipt is your proof.
